newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN FLUSH MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN FLUSH MARKET.

text.p: Short-term interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in Thursday's flush market, dealers said.
But local money dealers have predicted a general upward trend in the rates in January, when fewer treasury bill maturities -- a major source of liquidity in the market-- are anticipated.
On Thursday, treasury bills were being sold at 17.75 percent after closing at 17.85 percent on Tuesday, ahead of the new year break.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were selling in a 18 to 18.25 percentage range from 18.25 percent while bankers acceptance bills were quoted between 18.25 and 18.50 percent from 17.85 percent.
Call money fluctuated between 16.50 and 17.50 percent from around 18 percent in a market which opened Z$622 million in surplus, up from Z$40 million previously.
